title: Food scientist explains: tofu skin By @wendythefoodscientist Tofu ski...
description: Food scientist explains: tofu skin By @wendythefoodscientist Tofu skin, also known as yuba, beancurd skin, beancurd sheet, or beancurd robes, and as I know it: 腐竹 and 腐皮. Tofu skin is a traditional ingredient I grew up eating in Cantonese dishes like Buddha’s Delight and dim sum tofu skin rolls (腐皮卷), both shown in my video. In many countries, it’s hard to find tofu skin in stores. But here’s the good news: you can easily make it at home, with nothing but soy milk and patience. 💡 What is tofu skin? Tofu skin forms when you gently simmer fresh soy milk. As it heats, the proteins and fats naturally rise to the surface and bind together into a thin, delicate sheet. There’s no coagulant involved like in tofu. It’s just soy milk, heat, and time. You lift the skin off as it forms, let it dry slightly, and repeat — layer by layer. I think it is one of the most underrated soy foods so I am happy yo spread the word. 🍽️ How to use it: - Use fresh tofu skin to wrap fillings for dim sum rolls (腐皮卷) - Roll it up into sticks or layers — these are also known as 腐竹, or beancurd robes to create texture - If you’re using store-bought dried tofu skin, soak it first to rehydrate 📝 Recipe  1 L of homemade soy milk (see my soy milk video for my full method + tips) Method: 1️⃣ Pour soy milk into a wide, shallow pan. 2️⃣ Heat on low to medium-low — no boiling, just gentle steam. 3️⃣ Let a thin film form on top (5–10 min). Use a handheld fan to speed it up if you wish. 4️⃣ Gently lift the tofu skin with chopsticks, let it drip, and hang or lay flat to dry. 5️⃣ Repeat — you can get up to 16 sheets per liter depending on your pan size. 6️⃣ Use fresh, refrigerate for 2–3 days, or air dry completely to store for months. Follow me for more soy magic, from-scratch cooking, and food science that honours tradition #yuba #tofu #soymilk
